appearance_facts.fact: The title 'Incidence of Condition A in US States' is in large, bold, black text, positioned above the map.
A vertical color scale bar is located to the right of the map, labeled 'Low' at the bottom (dark red) and 'High' at the top (light yellow).
The state of Florida (FL) is colored dark red, indicating the highest incidence level on the map.
The state of New Hampshire (NH) is colored light yellow, indicating a low incidence level.
The state of Delaware (DE) is colored orange, indicating a moderate incidence level.
Several states including Idaho (ID), Wyoming (WY), and Minnesota (MN) are colored dark red, similar to Florida.
The state of Texas (TX) is colored light yellow, similar to New Hampshire.
The state of California (CA) is colored light gray, indicating no data or zero incidence.

printed_facts.fact: The chart title is 'Incidence of Condition A in US States'.
The legend is a vertical color bar with 'Low' at the bottom (dark red) and 'High' at the top (light yellow).
The map shows all 50 US states with two-letter postal abbreviations inside each state.
The color scale ranges from 0 to 100, with 0 at the bottom (dark red) and 100 at the top (light yellow).
States with dark red coloring (e.g., FL, ID, WY, MN) have the highest incidence values (near 100).
States with light yellow coloring (e.g., NH, TX, WA) have the lowest incidence values (near 0).
States with orange coloring (e.g., DE, NV, UT) have moderate incidence values (between 40 and 80).
States colored gray (e.g., CA, AL, AR) have no data or zero incidence.

public_definitions: The 'Highest-prevalence state statistics route' option should be selected based on the state with the highest incidence value on the map.
uncertain: The exact incidence value for each state is not provided in the map, only the color-coded relative ranking.
